ety.text: Attested since 2004. From вы- (vy-, “out-”) + русь (rusʹ, “Rus”); modeled on вы́крест (výkrest). Literally, “ex-Russian” or “no longer Russian”. Perhaps also a pun on вирус (virus).

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic истиньнъ (istinĭnŭ). By surface analysis, и́стина (ístina, “truth”) + -ный (-nyj).

ety.text: Borrowed from Dutch kooi or Middle Low German kōje, ultimately from Latin cavea. In sense of a normal bed when used in informal speech compare Swedish krypa till kojs and Norwegian Nynorsk krypa til køys.
